title: Transformers: Attention Is All You Need

blocks.title: The big picture
blocks.markdown:
The **transformer** is the neural network architecture behind modern AI — GPT, Claude, BERT, and nearly every frontier model. Introduced in the 2017 paper *Attention Is All You Need*, it replaced recurrence with a single powerful idea: **self-attention**, which lets every token in a sequence look at every other token directly.

Three properties made it take over the field:

- **Parallelism** — unlike RNNs, all positions are processed at once, so training scales across GPUs.
- **Long-range connections** — any token can attend to any other in one step, no matter the distance.
- **Scaling laws** — performance improves predictably as you add parameters and data.

By the end of this board you'll understand attention, the full architecture, how these models are trained, and where to go deeper.

blocks.title: Self-attention: queries, keys, values
blocks.tagline: Every word asks every other word: how relevant are you to me?
blocks.markdown:
Each token's embedding is projected into three vectors: a **query** (what am I looking for?), a **key** (what do I contain?), and a **value** (what do I contribute?).

Attention scores come from dot products of queries with keys, scaled and softmaxed:

```
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ / √d_k) · V
```

In *"The animal didn't cross the street because **it** was tired"*, the token `it` produces a query that matches the key of `animal` far more than `street` — so its output vector is built mostly from `animal`'s value. That's disambiguation, learned purely from data.

blocks.title: Multi-head attention
blocks.tagline: One attention pattern is never enough.
blocks.markdown:
Instead of a single attention function, the transformer runs **h parallel heads** (8 in the original paper), each with its own learned Q/K/V projections over a lower-dimensional subspace.

Different heads learn different relationships:

- one head tracks **syntax** (subject ↔ verb),
- another tracks **coreference** (pronoun ↔ noun),
- another watches **adjacent tokens**.

Their outputs are concatenated and projected back — giving the model many *representation subspaces* to reason in simultaneously.

blocks.title: Positional encoding
blocks.tagline: Attention is order-blind — position must be injected.
blocks.markdown:
Self-attention treats its input as a **set**: shuffle the tokens and the attention scores shuffle with them. Language obviously cares about order, so transformers add position information to each embedding.

- **Sinusoidal encodings** (the original): fixed sine/cosine waves of different frequencies.
- **Learned positional embeddings**: just train a vector per position.
- **RoPE (rotary)** — used by most modern LLMs: rotates Q/K vectors by an angle proportional to position, which elegantly encodes *relative* distances and extrapolates to longer contexts.

blocks.title: Self-attention in 20 lines of PyTorch
blocks.code:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def self_attention(x, W_q, W_k, W_v):
    """x: (seq_len, d_model) — one sequence, no batching for clarity."""
    Q = x @ W_q          # (seq, d_k)  what each token is looking for
    K = x @ W_k          # (seq, d_k)  what each token contains
    V = x @ W_v          # (seq, d_v)  what each token contributes

    d_k = Q.shape[-1]
    scores = Q @ K.T / d_k ** 0.5       # (seq, seq) relevance of j to i
    weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)  # rows sum to 1
    return weights @ V                   # blend values by relevance

seq_len, d_model, d_k = 6, 32, 16
x = torch.randn(seq_len, d_model)
W_q, W_k, W_v = (torch.randn(d_model, d_k) for _ in range(3))
print(self_attention(x, W_q, W_k, W_v).shape)  # torch.Size([6, 16])
blocks.explanation: The entire mechanism is three matrix multiplies, a scale, and a softmax. Causal (GPT-style) attention adds one line: mask the upper triangle of `scores` with `-inf` so tokens can't see the future.

blocks.title: Mental models that unlock it
blocks.markdown:
- **Attention is a soft dictionary lookup.** A query fuzzy-matches all keys and returns a weighted blend of values — differentiable, so it's learnable.
- **The FFN is where facts live; attention is where routing happens.** Roughly two-thirds of parameters are in feed-forward layers.
- **Residual stream as a shared whiteboard**: each layer reads from and writes small updates onto a running vector per token.
- **Beware the quadratic**: attention costs O(n²) in sequence length — this is why long context is hard and why FlashAttention, sliding windows, and sparse variants exist.

blocks.title: Going deeper: the frontier
blocks.markdown:
Where the research conversation is right now:

- **Efficient attention** — FlashAttention reorganizes the computation around GPU memory hierarchy; sliding-window and sparse patterns trade global view for O(n) cost.
- **Mixture-of-experts** — replace each FFN with many expert FFNs and route each token to a few; frontier models get more capacity per FLOP this way.
- **Long context** — RoPE scaling, attention sinks, and KV-cache compression push windows from 2K tokens (2019) to 1M+ (today).
- **Interpretability** — induction heads, superposition, and circuit analysis are beginning to explain *why* transformers generalize.

Open problems worth watching: reasoning beyond pattern matching, sample efficiency vs humans, and whether attention is the final architecture or just the current one.
